Dear Leo,
We visited the beach this morning. The sea was far from the rocks because the tide was low. Our guide showed us little pools between the rocks. My cousin wanted to put a small crab in her bucket. We washed our hands before lunch. We did not collect shells because some small animals might still be living in them.
Love,
Amy

Our class is making a shadow play about a bird. We put a white sheet across a frame and a lamp behind it. At first, the bird looked much larger than the paper tree. originalGroup.material:
Station Clock Letter 002

Dear Grandpa,
We almost missed our train yesterday. The clock above the waiting-room door stopped at ten twenty. Dad looked at it and said that we still had forty minutes. I checked the time on the station screen. It was already ten fifty. Our train was due at eleven. We asked a member of staff before running to a platform, because the platform number on our old ticket had changed. She directed us to Platform Four and called ahead for us. We arrived before boarding closed. Dad later reported the broken clock. He said a useful sign should be checked as carefully as a train. I was glad I looked at a second source instead of arguing about whose watch was right.
Love,
Ben

originalGroup.material:
Community Oven Letter 002

Dear Sara,
Our community kitchen has one large oven. Last month, two cooking groups arrived at the same time because one used a paper diary and the other used a phone calendar. Each thought its own booking was the only one. We now keep one booking board beside the kitchen door. A volunteer writes confirmed times on it after checking both groups’ requests. People can still ask by phone, so nobody needs a phone app. The board also includes ten minutes between groups for cleaning. Last Saturday, our bread took longer than expected. We told the next group early and helped clean the tables while it prepared its ingredients. The board cannot prevent every delay, but it makes the plan and the contact person clear.
Best wishes,
Nina

Our community kitchen has one large oven. Last month, two cooking groups arrived at the same time because one used a paper diary and the other used a phone calendar. Each thought its own booking was the only one. We now keep one booking board beside the kitchen door. A volunteer writes confirmed times on it after checking both groups’ requests. People can still ask by phone, so nobody needs a phone app. The board also includes ten minutes between groups for cleaning. Last Saturday, our bread took longer than expected. We told the next group early and helped clean the tables while it prepared its ingredients. The board cannot prevent every delay, but it makes the plan and the contact person clear.
Best wishes,
Nina
